Questions to ask a fishing guide before you book

Use a copyable fishing-guide inquiry and a quote comparison checklist. Confirm the target, departure, gear, license coverage and cancellation terms.

Source-checked · Updated 10 November 2026 · Castward editorial

Who this template suits

Use this page when you know the trip you want and need clear written answers from an operator. It differs from choosing a guide: this is the message and answer checklist for a specific proposed outing.

A clear inquiry helps a guide explain a suitable option. It does not create a booking. Castward’s planner prepares a draft that you can copy and send yourself.

When to send the inquiry

Send the first inquiry before buying tackle or nonrefundable travel. Include your available dates and any fixed commitments. Ask when the operator can confirm the final departure, target and weather plan.

After receiving a quote, send one follow-up for unresolved items. Reconfirm access, meeting details and current rules close to departure. Keep the written terms with your travel records.

Copy this inquiry and fill in the details

Hello. We are planning a fishing trip in [place] on [date or date range] for [party size]. Our experience is [level]. We prefer [target and method], and our maximum time away is [duration].

Please suggest a suitable trip and confirm the exact departure, boat or access method, time aboard and expected return. Our group needs [instruction, seating, shade, mobility support or other needs].

Please provide the total quote, deposit and balance dates, inclusions, exclusions and cancellation terms. What happens with unsuitable weather, an early return or a proposed substitute trip?

Please list the rods, tackle, clothing, safety equipment, food and transport you provide. Which sizes or personal items must we bring? What license coverage and permissions apply to our group?

How to compare the answers

Scroll the table to compare all columns.

QuestionUseful answerFollow up when
Where and how long?Named dock or access point, start and return, and travel portion.The answer says only “half day” or gives a broad region.
How will we fish?Named target, method, instruction and angler rotation.The answer promises fish without a practical plan.
What is included?Itemized equipment, bait, food, transport and exclusions.The answer says only “everything.”
What if conditions change?Written cancellation, early-return and substitute terms.The answer leaves payment and rescheduling unclear.

What to bring: ask for the personal list

Ask the operator to separate the guest list from the supplied equipment. Request footwear requirements, clothing guidance, food and water quantities, bag size and documents. Confirm any rental sizes.

For personal tackle, send the complete rod, reel and line details. Do not ask only whether you can bring “a fishing rod.” The answer needs the intended method and target.

What the guide provides: verify the actual service

Ask who leads the trip and which vessel or access format you will use. For a U.S. passenger charter, request the captain’s credential, safety plan and applicable vessel inspection information.

Confirm fishing-license coverage with the operator and the local authority. The Florida and North Carolina sources below show why coverage depends on the actual operation. They are examples, not a universal charter exemption.

Source: US Coast Guard: checks before a passenger charter · FWC: saltwater charter license coverage · NC DEQ: recreational fishing licenses

Mistakes to avoid in an inquiry

  • Omitting the least experienced guest’s needs.
  • Asking only for a price without a target, duration or party size.
  • Comparing a private boat with a shared seat as though they provide the same service.
  • Marking all gear provided after a vague answer.
  • Treating a draft inquiry as an accepted reservation.

Regulations and licenses

Ask the guide to name the relevant authority, waterbody and fishing permissions. Open the official rules yourself for the trip date. For the Situk planner example, use ADF&G’s regulations and emergency-order pages.

Do not store fees or limits from a quote as permanent rules. Keep current official links with the trip notes.

Source: ADF&G: fishing licenses · ADF&G: sport fishing regulations · ADF&G: emergency orders and news

Questions and answers

Does the planner send my inquiry to a guide?

No. It prepares a draft for you to copy and send. It does not reserve a boat or confirm a booking.

What should I ask before comparing prices?

Confirm the same target, method, duration, party size, access and provisions. Then compare the full written quotes.

What does “gear included” need to specify?

Ask for rods, reels, terminal tackle, bait or flies, clothing, footwear and safety equipment as named items, with sizes where relevant.

Sources and checked dates

Official source text checked on 10 November 2026. The packing lists and trip comparisons are Castward editorial advice. No local operator reviewed this article. It is not a field test or a live conditions report.

US Coast Guard: checks before a passenger charterChecked 2026-11-10

US Coast Guard bulletin of 7 September 2022. It advises passengers to check the captain’s credential, safety plan and applicable vessel inspection.

FWC: saltwater charter license coverageChecked 2026-11-10

Florida saltwater charter license scope. It does not confirm any individual operator or freshwater guest coverage.

NC DEQ: recreational fishing licensesChecked 2026-11-10

NC DEQ explains coastal recreational licenses and for-hire coverage. Confirm the coverage for the actual trip.

ADF&G: fishing licensesChecked 2026-11-10

ADF&G license directory. Confirm requirements for the individual traveler, species and trip.

ADF&G: sport fishing regulationsChecked 2026-11-10

ADF&G sport fishing regulations directory. Select Southeast Alaska and the named water, then check emergency orders.

ADF&G: emergency orders and newsChecked 2026-11-10

ADF&G emergency order search. Search the Yakutat management area immediately before the outing.
